title: 9 Best Herbal Tinctures For Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease
intro: Herbal tinctures for Peripheral arterial occlusive disease are natural liquid extracts made from plants and used to treat the condition characterized by the narrowing or blockage of arteries, leading to reduced blood flow to the limbs. The benefits of using herbal tinctures for this ailment include improved circulation, reduced inflammation, and enhanced overall cardiovascular health. Herbal tinctures such as Ginkgo biloba, which improves blood flow and reduces oxidative stress, and Turmeric, which reduces inflammation and improves cardiovascular health, have shown promise in treating Peripheral arterial occlusive disease. Additionally, herbal tinctures like Hawthorn, which improves cardiovascular health and reduces blood pressure, and Ginger, which reduces inflammation and improves circulation, may also be beneficial in managing this condition.

preparations.preparation_desc: Ginkgo biloba tinctures have been traditionally used to treat peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD) due to their vasodilatory and anti-inflammatory properties. The flavonoids and terpenoids present in Ginkgo biloba tinctures, such as quercetin, kaempferol, and bilobalide, help to improve blood circulation, reduce oxidative stress, and prevent platelet aggregation, thereby alleviating symptoms of PAOD. The bioactive constituents of Ginkgo biloba tinctures also help to increase nitric oxide production, which further enhances blood flow and reduces vascular resistance. Regular use of Ginkgo biloba tinctures has been shown to improve walking distance, reduce pain, and enhance overall quality of life in individuals with PAOD, making it a potential complementary therapy for this condition.
preparations.preparation_study: According to Arzneimittel-Forschung, Ginkgo biloba tinctures for peripheral arterial occlusive disease have been shown to improve pain-free walking distance, with a higher dosage of 240 mg daily resulting in a statistically significant increase of 107.0 m compared to the standard dosage of 120 mg daily, which resulted in a mean increase of 60.6 m.

preparations.preparation_study: According to "Journal of ethnopharmacology", Panax ginseng tinctures have been found to have a positive effect on inhibiting vascular intimal hyperplasia in peripheral arterial occlusive disease by reducing the protein expressions of the SDF-1α/CXCR4, SCF/c-kit and FKN/CX3CR1 axes.
